advances: Rigidity on a single fixed minimal face of the buffered maximizing base hull. The marked equality and actual cap cover give no joint deformation load inequality.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The energy root and the displayed power satisfy the buffer assumptions by the closed quantile-region theorem. Inclusion monotonicity and dilation covariance of d90ba05577427854 also give the marked functional hypotheses of the fixed-face cover theorem, with degree $d/(d+1)$, including the zero boundary extension. The balance and full tangent therefore exist with the stated shifted-own properness. By the fixed-face theorem, every point of $D_{q,\varepsilon}$ over $F_p$ is a full-tangent contact and each selected constraint is an equality. The set of such feasible points contains at least one over each vertex of $F_p$, since its vertices belong to $I$. Convexity gives a feasible point over every real base of $F_p$.

Let $F(z,X)=E_{C_z}(X)^{1/d}$, extended by zero. It is concave on $C$, and $f=F^\kappa$ for $\kappa=d/(d+1)\in(0,1)$. For any full-tangent contact over the face, its segment with $(p,y)$ lies in $C$. Concavity of $f$ and the affine upper bound force $f$ to be affine on that segment. At an interior segment parameter, concavity of $F$ and strict concavity of $t^\kappa$ on $[0,\infty)$ then force equal values of $F$ at the two endpoints and equality in the $F$ concavity inequality. The common value is positive because $y$ is own-interior. In particular the other mark is own-interior as well, so the equality theorem is applied only to interior marks.

For each such pair the containing-fiber version of 5aeb5916857f97a9 applies. The intermediate fiber contains the Minkowski combination by convexity of $C$, and the interpolated mark is interior by interpolating the two own inballs. Equality identifies the intermediate fiber with the entire Minkowski combination and makes the two centered endpoint bodies positive scalar multiples. Their equal positive energy and the dilation law of d90ba05577427854 make the scale factor one. Thus every full-tangent contact over a given base centers the fiber to $K_p-y$. Two such marks in the same fiber must coincide, because a nonempty bounded set cannot be invariant under a nonzero translation.

There is already a feasible contact over every real base on the face. Uniqueness identifies it with the full equality locus. Convexity of $D_{q,\varepsilon}$ now gives the affine interpolation of marks, and the identical centered bodies give the Minkowski interpolation of entire fibers, also for combinations with more than two endpoints. Translation gives constant volume, and equal energy was proved above. No differentiation of the cap masses is used.
statement:
Use the finite canonical mixed family and Euclidean buffered depth of the closed quantile-region theorem with $f(z,X)=E_{C_z}(X)^{1/(d+1)}$ extended by zero to own-fiber boundaries. Let $\varepsilon>0$, let $(p,y)$ be a sampled global buffered maximizer with $y\in\operatorname{int}K_p$ and $\varepsilon f(p,y)<\operatorname{dist}(y,\partial K_p)$, and put $q=Q_\varepsilon$. Let $I$ be the set of sampled maximizing bases and $F_p$ the minimal face of $\operatorname{conv}I$ containing $p$. Choose a positive-weight balanced mass-$q$ cap group at $(p,y)$ and a full supergradient extension $(\alpha,g)$ from the fixed-face cover theorem.

The part of $D_{q,\varepsilon}$ over $F_p$ is the graph of a unique affine mark $x(z)\in\operatorname{int}C_z$ at every real base $z\in F_p$. It is also exactly the full-tangent equality locus over that face. Every mark is an equality point of every selected buffered right-quantile constraint. The whole centered fibers $C_z-x(z)$, their volumes, and the values $E_{C_z}(x(z))$ are constant on the face. For any convex combination of bases $z=\sum_i\lambda_i z_i$ there, $C_z=\sum_i\lambda_i C_{z_i}$ and $x(z)=\sum_i\lambda_i x(z_i)$. The assertions include caps with nonregular supporting traces.
title: Whole-fiber equality at fixed buffered projective-energy contacts
